metadata.title: Aleksandar — Full-stack developer
metadata.description: Full-stack developer with a frontend focus, building fast interfaces in React and Next.js.

hero.heading: Aleksandar
hero.intro: I'm a full-stack developer with a frontend focus. I build considered, fast interfaces in React and Next.js — and the APIs, databases and deploys that keep them running.

services.heading: Three kinds of work, one way of working.
services.intro: Whichever you need, you get the same thing: something that loads fast, holds up, and is easy to hand over.

items.title: Websites
items.blurb: Marketing sites and landing pages that load fast, read well on a phone, and let you edit your own copy without calling me.

items.title: Web apps
items.blurb: Dashboards, portals and internal tools — auth, data, and the unglamorous flows that decide whether people actually use it.

items.title: Mobile apps
items.blurb: Cross-platform apps in React Native, shipped to both stores, that feel native rather than like a website in a shell.

paragraphs: Four years in, I've settled into the part of the stack I like most: the seam where a clean interface meets a system that actually holds up. Most of that time has been React and Next.js on the front, Node and Postgres behind it.

I care about the small things — how a page loads, how a form fails, whether the thing you clicked feels like it responded. AI and agentic tools are a normal part of how I work now; they handle the scaffolding so I can spend my attention on architecture and detail. I write in plain language, ship in small increments, and I'd rather ask one more question than build the wrong thing.
about.callout: Right now I'm open to both a full-time role and freelance builds — websites, web apps, or mobile.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.blurb: A call and a short written brief. I want to know who it's for and what success looks like before I open an editor.

steps.title: Design
steps.blurb: Wireframes first, then real screens. You see it early and often, so nothing lands as a surprise.

steps.title: Build
steps.blurb: Small increments on a live preview URL. I lean on AI and agentic tools for scaffolding and tests, which buys back time for the details that matter.

steps.title: Launch
steps.blurb: Deploy, analytics, a walkthrough and clean docs — then a check-in once you've lived with it.

projects.intro: Recent work — real projects, not demos.

items.title: Plava Laguna Partners Portal
items.blurb: A login-protected portal for Plava Laguna's travel-agency partners — property listings, fact sheets and photos in one place, filterable by type, stars and location. Content runs through Contentful, so the team edits it without touching code.

items.title: Celeste
items.blurb: An astronomy learning app — spaced-repetition flashcards, constellation quizzes, and a live AR sky view that shows tonight's planets and meteor showers through the camera. Levels, XP and streaks make it stick.

items.title: Focus Flow
items.blurb: A mobile task manager — Today, Board and Categories screens, one Kanban flow from todo to done, and due-date reminders. Built on Supabase auth and Postgres, everything scoped to your account.

items.title: Posavski Med
items.blurb: A marketing site for a family beekeeping business in Posavina — product range, the family's story and a blog, built to earn trust and turn visitors into contacts. Fully static, no backend.

faq.heading: The things clients usually ask first.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A marketing site is usually two to three weeks. A web or mobile app depends on scope — most of what I take on lands between six and ten weeks. I'll give you a range after our first call, and I'd rather revise it out loud than quietly miss it.
Fixed price when the scope is clear, a weekly rate when it isn't yet. Either way you see the number before I start, and there are no surprise line items at the end.

items.q: Do you work with existing teams?
items.a: Often. I'm comfortable dropping into an existing codebase, following your conventions, and reviewing PRs rather than rewriting things. I ask a lot of questions in the first week and fewer after that.

items.q: What if I only need part of a project?
items.a: That's fine — plenty of my work is one slice: a frontend on top of an API you already have, a design handed to me as Figma files, or a performance and accessibility pass on something already live.

items.q: Do you keep working on it after launch?
items.a: If you want me to. I'll hand over clean docs so you're not dependent on me, and I'm happy to stay on a small monthly arrangement for fixes and small features.

contact.intro: Hiring, freelance, or just a question about a stack decision — I reply to everything.
